_note: Evergreen segments for a thin week (plan §4.6; launch-cohort review 2026-09-23). Each is a standing explainer about how the town and the south Georgian Bay region work — never a news item, never a claim about this week. Written to be true for a season, reviewed each quarter. Mira reads them as background, sourced to the public bodies named inside.

segments.title: How Collingwood Council Makes a Decision
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on how a decision moves through the Town of Collingwood's council: the committee-of-the-whole stage, the regular council meeting, public deputations and how a resident registers to speak, the role of staff reports, and when a by-law takes effect. Name the Town of Collingwood as the source of the procedure and say where the agendas are published. No opinion, no reference to any current item.

segments.title: What the Town Does and What the County Does
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on the split of responsibilities between the Town of Collingwood and the County of Simcoe: roads (which are county roads, which are town roads, and who plows which), waste and recycling, paramedics, social housing and Ontario Works, land-use planning appeals, and the library. Name both bodies as the sources. No opinion, no reference to any current item.

segments.title: Why Water Capacity Decides What Gets Built
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on why drinking-water and wastewater treatment capacity sets the pace of new housing in Collingwood: how servicing allocation works, what an interim control by-law is, why capacity is counted in equivalent residential units, and where the Town publishes its allocation decisions. Name the Town of Collingwood as the source. Explain the mechanism without referring to any specific current application or developer.

segments.title: Who Clears Which Road When the Snow Comes
segments.prompt_template: Write a 220-300 word explainer on winter road maintenance around south Georgian Bay: provincial highways (Highway 26, Highway 124) and the Ministry of Transportation's classes, county roads and the County of Simcoe's service levels, town streets and sidewalks and the Town of Collingwood's priority routes, and where a listener checks conditions (Ontario 511 and the local road-closure pages). No forecast, no reference to a specific storm.

segments.title: The Harbour and the Shipyards: How the Waterfront Is Governed
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on who governs Collingwood's waterfront: the Town's ownership of the harbour lands, the federal role in navigable waters, the Waterfront Master Plan as a standing document, the terminals and grain elevator as a heritage question, and how a resident finds the plan and its public meetings. Name the Town of Collingwood as the source. Background only, no current proposal.

segments.title: Four School Boards, One Town
segments.prompt_template: Write a 220-300 word explainer on the four school boards that serve Collingwood and area families — the Simcoe County District School Board, the Simcoe Muskoka Catholic District School Board, and the two French-language boards — what each governs, how trustees are elected, and where board meeting agendas are published. Name the boards as sources. No reference to any current board decision.

segments.title: How a Hospital Gets Rebuilt in Ontario
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on the Ontario capital planning process a hospital redevelopment goes through — the stages from proposal to functional program to construction, the split between provincial funding and the local share a community must raise, and the role of the hospital foundation — using Collingwood General and Marine Hospital's redevelopment as the standing local example only for the fact that it exists. Name Ontario Health and the hospital as sources. No timeline claims about the current project.

segments.title: The Escarpment Rules: Why Some Land Can't Be Built On
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on the Niagara Escarpment Plan and the Niagara Escarpment Commission as they apply to the Blue Mountains and the south Georgian Bay slopes: the land-use designations, what a development permit is, how the plan interacts with municipal zoning, and where the maps are published. Name the Commission as the source. Background only.

segments.title: How Short-Term Rental Licensing Works Here
segments.prompt_template: Write a 220-300 word explainer on how short-term accommodation is licensed in the Town of Collingwood and the Town of The Blue Mountains: the licence categories, the difference between the two municipalities' regimes, what a complaint process looks like, and where the by-laws are published. Name both towns as sources. No reference to a specific property or current enforcement case.

segments.title: Why Georgian Bay's Water Level Rises and Falls
segments.prompt_template: Write a 250-350 word explainer on Lake Huron–Georgian Bay water levels: the seasonal cycle, the multi-year swings, what the International Joint Commission and Environment and Climate Change Canada measure and publish, and what a high or low year means for harbours, beaches and shoreline property. Name the Commission and the department as sources. No forecast for this year.

segments.title: Where a Collingwood Property-Tax Dollar Goes
segments.prompt_template: Write a 220-300 word explainer on how a residential property-tax bill in Collingwood is built: the town levy, the County of Simcoe levy, the provincial education portion, how MPAC assessment feeds the calculation, and when the budget that sets the town rate is normally debated. Name the Town, the County and MPAC as sources. Mechanism only, no figures for the current year.

segments.title: Getting Around Without a Car: Colltrans and LINX
segments.prompt_template: Write a 220-300 word explainer on public transit in and around Collingwood: the Town's Colltrans routes, the County's LINX regional service between Collingwood, Wasaga Beach and Barrie, how fares and schedules are published, and how the two connect. Name the Town of Collingwood and the County of Simcoe as sources. No service-change claims.
